verdict.rationale: DBOS's own architecture keeps all workflow state in a Postgres database you supply, and it documents self-hosting Conductor and the DBOS Console on your own infrastructure. That means data location follows wherever you deploy, which is real but implicit residency control rather than a dedicated region/residency feature. missing for 10: explicit region/residency selection for DBOS-managed Conductor/Cloud, documented data-residency guarantees or compliance statements, independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can choose where my data is stored (region/residency)

citations.quote: There's no separate orchestration server and no infrastructure required besides Postgres.
DBOS checkpoints those workflows and steps to a Postgres database.
There are many ways to self-host Conductor and the DBOS Console on your own infrastructure
against DBOS-managed Conductor or a self-hosted Conductor
